title: Well-definedness of F_s as a cubical CW complex (resolution preserves coherence)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Gap A.** The construction of $F_s$ in the problem statement must be verified to be a genuine CW (cubical) complex.

Specifically prove:
1. Resolving a $k$-crossing matching $M$ at a crossing $c$ in either local manner $a\in\partial I_c$ yields a matching $M_a$ with crossing set EXACTLY $X(M_a)=X(M)\setminus\{c\}$ (resolution at $c$ neither creates nor destroys other crossings, up to isotopy).
2. $M_a$ is still a **coherent** matching, i.e. it satisfies the region condition: for each component $R$ of $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}_+\setminus M_a$ and each boundary arc $A$, $\partial A=\{(i,0),(j,0)\}$ with $w_i=w_j^{-1}$. This is the nontrivial part: resolving a crossing merges/splits complementary regions, and coherence must be shown stable under this.
3. The face map sends the facet $a\times\prod_{d\neq c}I_d$ to $C(M_a)=\prod_{d\in X(M_a)}I_d$ canonically and consistently, so that boundaries of cubes map into the lower skeleton and the gluing is well-defined and continuous.

Without this lemma, statements such as 'the complex has three 2-cells' are not well-posed. Analogous to verifying the Khovanov/Bar-Natan cube of resolutions is a legitimate complex.

comments.author: solver-agent
comments.body:
**Resolved.** Added a new subsection *"Well-definedness of $F_s$ as a cubical CW complex"* to `solution.tex` proving the three required points (W1)-(W3).

**(W1) Locality (Lemma `lem:W1`).** Resolution at $c$ is supported in a small disk $D_c$ meeting $M$ in exactly the two crossing chords; smoothing replaces the "X" by two disjoint chords with the same four boundary germs. Since $M=M_a$ outside $D_c$ and $M_a\cap D_c$ has no crossing, $X(M_a)=X(M)\setminus\{c\}$ exactly. Purely geometric, no coherence needed.

**(W2) Coherence preserved (Prop `prop:W2`).** The nontrivial part. Anatomy lemma `lem:shapeA` (from the existing Lemma `lem:bigon`): each boundary component $A$ of a region in a coherent matching is an embedded arc turning corners at crossings, running between $x$-axis ends $(i,0),(j,0)$ with $w_i=w_j^{-1}$. Local analysis: smoothing merges two opposite sectors into one region $R_{24}$ and reshapes $R_1,R_3$. The core (Lemma `lem:splice`) is an **honest direct tracking of boundary components** — explicitly NOT an isotopy $M_a\simeq M$ (a smoothing genuinely changes the 1-manifold). Type-coloring the germs ($\alpha^\pm=\mathsf A,\ \beta^\pm=\mathsf B$): coherence forces all four germ-ends to carry one letter up to sign, $\mathsf A\mapsto\ell,\ \mathsf B\mapsto\ell^{-1}$. Persisting regions inherit inverse ends. For $R_{24}$ I show its frontier is the single 4-cycle $\alpha^+\xrightarrow{\gamma}\beta^+\xrightarrow{\partial R_2}\alpha^-\xrightarrow{\delta}\beta^-\xrightarrow{\partial R_4}\alpha^+$ whose types alternate $\mathsf A\mathsf B\mathsf A\mathsf B$; each maximal arc-portion joins adjacent germs, hence opposite type, hence inverse letters. No all-arc circle arises. So $M_a$ is coherent.

**Corollary `cor:dimdrop`:** coherent + (W1) + bigon-freeness gives $\dim C(M_a)=\dim C(M)-1$. I verified by computer the genuine subtlety: the naive "smooth a crossing" can drop the interleaving count by MORE than one — precisely in the triangle config (three pairwise-interleaving arcs) — but that config is exactly the incoherent one (its triangular region has all-arc boundary, contra Lemma bigon), so it never arises from a coherent input. The apparent over-drop corresponds to a bigon in the non-minimal $M_a$, forbidden by coherence. This is why coherence is the linchpin.

**(W3) Consistent face maps (Lemmas `lem:facemap`, `lem:commute`, Prop `prop:W3`).** Each facet maps to $C(M_{c,a})$ by the identity on the untouched coordinates $X(M)\setminus\{c\}$. Resolutions at distinct crossings commute (disjoint disks), so codim-2 faces match in both orders; facet maps agree on overlaps and glue to a continuous attaching map $\varphi_M:\partial C(M)\to F_s^{(k-1)}$, a homeomorphism onto a subcomplex — the regular-CW (cubical) condition. Degreewise finiteness holds since coherent matchings are determined by their pairings.

This makes the Solution's cell counts and attaching data well-posed. (No LaTeX toolchain available to compile, but environment/reference balance of `solution.tex` was validated.) Closing as resolved.
